summary: On node1 (Alpine 3.23), created the `datauser` account, provisioned a dedicated 300MB loopback ext4 filesystem (native ext4 quota feature enabled via tune2fs) mounted at /srv/data (persisted in /etc/fstab with usrquota,grpquota), owned by datauser, and applied a filesystem-enforced user quota of 100MB (102400 1K-blocks, soft=hard) for datauser via setquota. Verified enforcement: writes up to ~99MB succeed, writes beyond 100MB fail at the kernel/filesystem level with "Quota exceeded" (ENOSPC-style EDQUOT), independent of any application logic. Added /etc/local.d/srv-data-quota.start (enabled in the default OpenRC runlevel) to guarantee quotaon runs at boot. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, quota state, mount, and a data marker file; issued a native reboot; polled until node1 was reachable again; confirmed boot_id changed (412576a1... -> 11f48b77...); confirmed the /srv/data mount, quota accounting/enforcement, and marker file all recovered automatically without any manual intervention; re-ran the over-quota write test post-restart and confirmed it still fails as expected.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/filesystem (Alpine 3.23, ext4 root, no existing /srv/data or datauser)
Installed quota-tools and e2fsprogs via apk
Created a 300MB loopback image, formatted ext4, enabled native ext4 quota feature via tune2fs -O quota
Added persistent fstab entry mounting the loop image at /srv/data with usrquota,grpquota
Enabled quota accounting (quotaon) and set setquota -u datauser 102400 102400 0 0 /srv/data (100MB soft=hard)
Verified enforcement: 150MB write as datauser stopped at ~99MB with 'Quota exceeded'; 50MB write succeeded and was cleaned up
Configured /etc/local.d/srv-data-quota.start + rc-update add local default to keep quota enabled across boots
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, mount state, quota state/report, fstab, and a persistence marker file written as datauser
Issued a native reboot (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect), polled until node1 exec was available again
Verified changed boot_id post-restart, and confirmed mount, quota enforcement (repeated over-quota write test), and marker file all recovered automatically
Cleaned up test files, left /srv/data in a clean state with datauser quota active

evidence.requirement: datauser account created and limited to 100MB under /srv/data, enforced by the filesystem
evidence.summary: datauser created (uid 1001); dedicated ext4 loop filesystem mounted at /srv/data with native ext4 quota; setquota applied 102400/102400 1K-block (100MB) soft/hard limit; dd write of 150MB stopped by kernel at ~99MB with 'Quota exceeded', 50MB write succeeded, confirming filesystem-level enforcement
fstab entry for /srv/data loop mount with usrquota,grpquota added; /etc/local.d/srv-data-quota.start created and 'local' service enabled in default runlevel, running after localmount
Captured boot_id 412576a1-ff92-42f3-9415-2cd15e7ab4d0, /srv/data mount with quota options active, repquota showing datauser 100MB limit, and wrote marker.txt as datauser as a data-integrity baseline

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged and returned before disconnect; subsequent polls timed out/reset while node was down; node1 became reachable again with new boot_id 11f48b77-4e67-4f41-8df0-444945c4c304, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery of required services/data and quota enforcement
evidence.summary: After restart, /srv/data auto-remounted with quota options, quota accounting was on, repquota showed the same 100MB limit for datauser, marker.txt was intact, and a repeat 150MB write test again failed at ~99MB with 'Quota exceeded', confirming full recovery of the enforced quota
